analysis_questions.prompt: Record two specific observations of the anchoring phenomenon for biological scale and measurement and one thing that does not yet fit your explanation. Apply biological scale and measurement to a case in Scientific Practice, Measurement, and the Molecules of Life you have not worked before. Show the reasoning that produced your result, not only the result, and name the single step where that reasoning is most likely to break down.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming individual protein molecules can be resolved with a light microscope.
Reporting a biological measurement with no unit, or with a unit off by orders of magnitude for the structure named.
Claiming a cell and an organelle are of comparable size.
fixed_facts: Typical bacterial cells are on the order of micrometres; typical eukaryotic cells are tens of micrometres; molecules such as proteins are on the order of nanometres.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Electron microscopy theory, super-resolution methods, and instrument physics are beyond this course.
relationships: Biological structures span many orders of magnitude, and the appropriate unit and instrument change with the scale being studied.
The scale of a structure constrains what can be observed about it: light microscopy resolves cells and large organelles, not individual proteins.
A measurement is meaningful only with its unit and the method that produced it.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming an enzyme is used up in the reaction it catalyses.
Claiming an enzyme makes an energetically unfavourable reaction favourable.
Claiming high temperature always increases enzyme activity, ignoring denaturation.
fixed_facts: An enzyme lowers the activation energy of a reaction and is not consumed by it.
Enzymes do not change whether a reaction is energetically favourable; they change how fast it proceeds.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Enzyme kinetics, Michaelis-Menten parameters, and inhibition types are beyond this course.
relationships: An enzyme is a biological catalyst: it lowers activation energy, speeds the reaction, and emerges unchanged.
Enzyme activity depends on temperature and pH, rising to an optimum and falling away as the enzyme's shape is disrupted.
Specificity comes from the shape and chemistry of the active site, which is why an enzyme acts on particular substrates.

safety_brief.h3_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): 3% hydrogen peroxide irritates eyes and can bleach fabric and skin on contact.
MITIGATION: Use the household 3% strength only, keep it in its original bottle, wear eye protection, work over a washable surface, and rinse any splash with water for 15 minutes.
HAZARD (chemical): Hydrogen peroxide and lemon juice must never be combined; together they make peracetic acid, which is corrosive and irritating to the airway.
MITIGATION: The lemon-juice route and the peroxide route run in separate labelled cups. They are never poured together, never poured into a shared waste cup, and never combined to see what happens.
HAZARD (chemical): Catalase and peroxide foam vigorously and release oxygen.
MITIGATION: No lid, cap, film, or cover ever goes on a peroxide container. Use a wide open cup on a tray with plenty of headroom.
HAZARD (physical): Slicing produce with a kitchen knife risks cuts.
MITIGATION: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses pre-cut produce; no knife work is required by the lesson.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Put on eye protection and lay everything out on a washable tray before any container is opened.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult does all cutting; the learner takes only pre-cut produce.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run the no-chemical browning comparison first - air, water, wrapped - and record it before any chemical appears.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Only then, if the catalase route runs, an adult pours 3% hydrogen peroxide into its own labelled open cup and caps the bottle.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep the lemon-juice cups and the peroxide cups apart on the tray. Never pour one into the other, and never put a lid on a peroxide cup.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if hydrogen peroxide contacts the eyes and rinse for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Stop if anyone moves to combine the peroxide and the lemon juice, or to cap a peroxide container.
  STOP: Stop if any cut occurs and treat it before continuing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the peroxide and the lemon-juice cups down the drain SEPARATELY, each with the cold tap running, and never into a shared waste cup. Wash the cups, compost or bin the produce, and wash hands. Nothing is ever capped or sealed, and nothing is kept or reused.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the browning comparison with no chemicals at all: compare apple slices in air, under water, and wrapped, timing colour change against a printed colour scale. This needs only produce, water, and a timer and meets the same target.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming individual protein molecules can be resolved with a light microscope.
Reporting a biological measurement with no unit, or with a unit off by orders of magnitude for the structure named.
Claiming a cell and an organelle are of comparable size.
fixed_facts: Typical bacterial cells are on the order of micrometres; typical eukaryotic cells are tens of micrometres; molecules such as proteins are on the order of nanometres.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Electron microscopy theory, super-resolution methods, and instrument physics are beyond this course.
relationships: Biological structures span many orders of magnitude, and the appropriate unit and instrument change with the scale being studied.

A measurement is meaningful only with its unit and the method that produced it.

safety_brief.h3_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): 3% hydrogen peroxide irritates eyes and can bleach fabric and skin on contact.
MITIGATION: Use the household 3% strength only, keep it in its original bottle, wear eye protection, work over a washable surface, and rinse any splash with water for 15 minutes.
HAZARD (chemical): Hydrogen peroxide and lemon juice must never be combined; together they make peracetic acid, which is corrosive and irritating to the airway.
MITIGATION: The lemon-juice route and the peroxide route run in separate labelled cups. They are never poured together, never poured into a shared waste cup, and never combined to see what happens.
HAZARD (chemical): Catalase and peroxide foam vigorously and release oxygen.
MITIGATION: No lid, cap, film, or cover ever goes on a peroxide container. Use a wide open cup on a tray with plenty of headroom.
HAZARD (physical): Slicing produce with a kitchen knife risks cuts.
MITIGATION: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses pre-cut produce; no knife work is required by the lesson.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Put on eye protection and lay everything out on a washable tray before any container is opened.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult does all cutting; the learner takes only pre-cut produce.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Run the no-chemical browning comparison first - air, water, wrapped - and record it before any chemical appears.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Only then, if the catalase route runs, an adult pours 3% hydrogen peroxide into its own labelled open cup and caps the bottle.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep the lemon-juice cups and the peroxide cups apart on the tray. Never pour one into the other, and never put a lid on a peroxide cup.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if hydrogen peroxide contacts the eyes and rinse for 15 minutes.
  STOP: Stop if anyone moves to combine the peroxide and the lemon juice, or to cap a peroxide container.
  STOP: Stop if any cut occurs and treat it before continuing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the peroxide and the lemon-juice cups down the drain SEPARATELY, each with the cold tap running, and never into a shared waste cup. Wash the cups, compost or bin the produce, and wash hands. Nothing is ever capped or sealed, and nothing is kept or reused.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the browning comparison with no chemicals at all: compare apple slices in air, under water, and wrapped, timing colour change against a printed colour scale. This needs only produce, water, and a timer and meets the same target.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming carbon forms a number of covalent bonds other than four in these molecules.
Claiming lipids are polymers of a repeating monomer in the way proteins and nucleic acids are.
Claiming monomers are joined by adding water and separated by removing it.
fixed_facts: Carbon forms four covalent bonds, which is why it builds the large, varied molecules life depends on.
The four major classes of biological macromolecule are carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Detailed organic reaction mechanisms and stereochemistry are Chemistry course work.
relationships: Carbon's capacity to form four stable covalent bonds, including with other carbon atoms, allows chains, branches, and rings, and therefore enormous molecular variety.
Carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids are polymers built from repeating monomers; lipids are not polymers in the same sense.
Monomers are joined by removing water and separated by adding it.

Specificity comes from the shape and chemistry of the active site, which is why an enzyme acts on particular substrates.

disqualifying_errors: Pairing adenine with guanine, or cytosine with thymine.
Claiming the bases form the backbone and the sugars and phosphates lie in the interior.
Claiming the two strands run in the same direction.
fixed_facts: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.
DNA is a double helix of two antiparallel strands with a sugar-phosphate backbone on the outside and paired bases on the inside.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Base-stacking energetics, DNA topology, and chromatin structure in detail are beyond this course.
relationships: DNA is composed of nucleotides, each a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and one of four nitrogenous bases.
The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases: adenine with thymine, guanine with cytosine.
Because the pairing is complementary, each strand specifies the sequence of the other, which is what makes accurate copying possible.

disqualifying_errors: Pairing adenine with guanine, or cytosine with thymine.
Claiming the bases form the backbone and the sugars and phosphates lie in the interior.
Claiming the two strands run in the same direction.
fixed_facts: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.
DNA is a double helix of two antiparallel strands with a sugar-phosphate backbone on the outside and paired bases on the inside.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Base-stacking energetics, DNA topology, and chromatin structure in detail are beyond this course.
relationships: DNA is composed of nucleotides, each a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and one of four nitrogenous bases.
The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases: adenine with thymine, guanine with cytosine.
Because the pairing is complementary, each strand specifies the sequence of the other, which is what makes accurate copying possible.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming RNA contains thymine.
Claiming transcription produces protein.
Claiming every gene is transcribed in every cell at all times.
fixed_facts: Transcription copies a DNA sequence into RNA; RNA contains uracil in place of thymine and ribose in place of deoxyribose.
In eukaryotes transcription occurs in the nucleus and translation occurs at ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Promoter structure, splicing detail, and transcription factor biochemistry are beyond this course.
relationships: Transcription produces a single-stranded RNA copy complementary to one DNA strand.
Only part of the genome is transcribed in any given cell at any given time, which is why cells with identical DNA differ.
The messenger RNA carries the sequence information out of the nucleus to the ribosome.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming prokaryotic cells have no DNA or no ribosomes.
Claiming viruses are cells or are alive by the criteria of cell theory.
Claiming cells can arise spontaneously from non-living material under present conditions.
fixed_facts: All living organisms are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have both.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Endosymbiotic theory in detail and archaeal biology are beyond this course.
relationships: Cell theory holds that organisms are composed of cells, that the cell is the basic unit of structure and function, and that cells arise only from existing cells.
Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and a range of organelles.
Both cell types have a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, and DNA.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming plant cells have chloroplasts instead of mitochondria; plant cells have both.
Claiming mitochondria produce energy rather than converting it into a usable chemical form.
Claiming organelles function independently of one another.
fixed_facts: The nucleus holds the genetic material, ribosomes assemble proteins, mitochondria carry out most ATP production, and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis in plant cells.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Vesicular trafficking detail and organelle proteomics are beyond this course.
relationships: Organelles are specialised compartments whose functions depend on one another, so the cell operates as an integrated system.
Membranes create separate chemical environments, which is what allows incompatible processes to run in the same cell at once.
A product of one organelle is frequently the input of another, so disrupting one disrupts others.

safety_brief.h3_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Cutting cubes to size uses a knife.
MITIGATION: An adult does all cutting, or the learner uses clay shaped by hand with no cutting tool.
HAZARD (physical): Microscope lamps get warm and slides have sharp edges.
MITIGATION: Handle slides by their edges, let the lamp cool before storage, and treat the microscope step as optional.
HAZARD (physical): Broken slide glass cuts whoever empties the bin.
MITIGATION: An adult sweeps fragments with stiff card, wraps them in thick paper and tape, and bins them separately. Never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Clear and wipe the work surface before anything is set out.
  SAFE ORDER 2. An adult does every cut; the learner receives pre-cut cubes or shapes clay by hand with no cutting tool.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Measure and record every cube before any liquid is added.
  SAFE ORDER 4. If the microscope route runs, an adult mounts the slide and the learner handles it by its edges only.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Switch the lamp off and let it cool before anything is packed away.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if a slide chips or breaks and let an adult clear it as described.
  STOP: Stop if anyone reaches for a knife; all cutting is done by an adult.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Clay goes back into its container and potato cubes into the compost or bin; pour coloured water down the drain and rinse the containers. An adult clears any broken slide by sweeping the fragments with stiff card, wrapping them in thick paper and tape, and binning them separately - never by hand, never loose, never with a vacuum cleaner.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the whole unit with no microscope and no cutting: use published, openly licensed onion-root-tip micrographs to count cells in each mitotic phase, and model surface-area-to-volume with hand-rolled clay cubes measured with a ruler.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

DISPOSAL: Pour the cooled water down the drain, dry the containers, and return the plants to their usual place. No sample and no body or health measurement is taken or kept.

ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.

  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a homeostatically regulated variable is held perfectly constant.
Treating any fluctuation within the tolerance range as a regulatory failure.
Claiming all regulated variables share one tolerance range.
fixed_facts: Homeostasis maintains internal conditions within a tolerance range, not at a single unchanging value.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Control theory and quantitative physiological modelling are beyond this course.
relationships: A regulated variable has a setpoint and a range within which the organism functions.
Values fluctuate within the range continuously; regulation acts when a departure is detected, so variation is expected.
Different variables have different ranges, and exceeding a range has consequences specific to that variable.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming atoms are consumed or destroyed during metabolism.
Claiming body mass lost is converted into energy and thereby ceases to be matter.
Claiming an organism builds tissue from matter that did not enter it.
fixed_facts: Atoms are conserved through every metabolic process; they are rearranged, never created or destroyed.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Isotope tracer methodology and metabolic flux analysis are beyond this course.
relationships: The atoms in an organism's body came from the food, water, and gases it took in.
Tracing an element through metabolism means following where its atoms go, and every atom is accounted for.
Mass lost by an organism leaves as matter, principally as exhaled carbon dioxide and as water, not as energy.

instruction:
Focus for today: light energy capture, inside the unit Photosynthesis, Cellular Respiration, and Energy in Living Systems.
Anchoring phenomenon: A large tree grows tonnes of wood while the soil beneath it barely loses mass.
Unit question: Where does the matter in a tree come from, and where does the energy in your food actually go?
What you are aiming at: Plan and carry out a safe investigation of light energy capture, or its stated alternative, and record the learner's own data with its uncertainty. Explain light energy capture using evidence, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer. Apply light energy capture to a task the learner has not seen before, showing the reasoning that produced the result. Check and revise the work on light energy capture against the stated success criteria and name the next step.
You have met the target when: The learner completes the central task about light energy capture. The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process, not a bare answer. The learner checks or revises the work and identifies one specific next step. Any quantity the learner reports is one the learner measured, computed, or cited to a named published source. The learner states the investigation's limitations and what the data cannot show. The learner records the safety review and the supervision that was actually in place.
The work itself: SAFETY FIRST - SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there. Read the safety review segment in full before you touch any material, follow the safe order in the order written, stop at once if any stop condition happens, and finish with the disposal steps. Work through the safe order in the safety review, in order, without reordering it. Stop at once if any stop condition happens. Then run the remaining trials and record your own data. No expected value is supplied beforehand and no result is ever filled in for you. If the data is messy, write down what happened and why it may have happened. Finish with the disposal steps in the safety review before anything is packed away.

safety_brief.h3_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (chemical): Baking soda solution irritates eyes.
MITIGATION: Wear eye protection and rinse any splash with water.
HAZARD (physical): A lamp close to a water container gets hot and mixes electricity with water.
MITIGATION: Use an LED lamp only - never incandescent or halogen, which crack a cup and can ignite paper at this distance. Keep it at least 30 cm away, never above the water, and plug it in away from any spill zone; an adult positions the lamp.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water scalds, and hot tap water kills the yeast anyway.
MITIGATION: An adult mixes the yeast water and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 40 degrees Celsius. Temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
HAZARD (physical): A syringe with a needle, or a blocked tip under vacuum, injures or sprays.
MITIGATION: Use a needleless blunt-tip syringe only. No needle of any kind is used in this course.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
EYE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED for this investigation. Put it on before the first step.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult positions the LED lamp first, at least 30 cm from any container and never above it, with the cord away from the spill zone.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Fill and place the containers only after the lamp is fixed in position.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult mixes the yeast water and confirms with the thermometer that it reads below 40 degrees Celsius before yeast is added.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Fit the balloon loosely so gas can escape; never seal a fermenting container.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Switch the lamp off and let it cool before any container is moved or emptied.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop immediately if any liquid reaches a lamp, cord, or outlet.
  STOP: Stop if a sealed container bulges; never fully seal a fermenting container.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the baking-soda and yeast mixtures down the drain with the tap running, compost or bin the leaf material, wash the containers with soap, and wash hands. Leave any yeast container open until fizzing stops before it is binned. Nothing is sealed, kept, or stored.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the yeast-and-sugar respiration comparison with a loosely fitted balloon and no lamp at all, or analyse a published photosynthesis-rate dataset against light intensity. Both meet the matter-and-energy target with kitchen materials or paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming chlorophyll absorbs green light most strongly.
Claiming plants take in light and store it as light energy.
Claiming photosynthesis occurs in the mitochondria.
fixed_facts: Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the blue and red regions and reflects green, which is why plants appear green.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Photosystem biochemistry, electron transport detail, and absorption spectra analysis are beyond this course.
relationships: Pigments absorb particular wavelengths of light and transfer that energy into the photosynthetic process.
Light absorbed is used; light reflected or transmitted is not, which is why leaf colour indicates which wavelengths are least used.
The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming energy cycles through an ecosystem the way matter does.
Claiming most of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next.
Claiming a long food chain supports as much biomass at the top as at the bottom.
fixed_facts: Only a small fraction of the energy at one trophic level, on the order of ten per cent, is incorporated into the next.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Quantitative production ecology and ecological efficiency measurement are beyond this course.
relationships: Energy enters most ecosystems through producers and passes upward through consumers, with most released as thermal energy at each transfer.
Because so little energy passes upward, food chains have few levels and higher levels support far less biomass.
Energy flows through an ecosystem in one direction and is not recycled.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming plants take nitrogen directly from the air.
Claiming animals obtain nitrogen from the atmosphere.
Claiming adding more nutrients to an ecosystem always improves it.
fixed_facts: Atmospheric nitrogen gas cannot be used directly by plants or animals; it must first be fixed into usable compounds.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Detailed microbial biochemistry and nutrient-loading models are beyond this course.
relationships: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and industrial processes, convert atmospheric nitrogen into forms plants can take up.
Nitrogen moves from soil to plants to consumers and back through excretion and decomposition.
Adding excess nutrients to water bodies stimulates growth that, on decomposing, depletes dissolved oxygen.

fixed_facts: Exponential growth has no limiting factor and cannot be sustained; logistic growth slows as the population approaches carrying capacity.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a population can sustain exponential growth indefinitely.
Claiming logistic growth means the population stops changing once it reaches carrying capacity.
Confusing the growth rate with the population size.
fixed_facts: Exponential growth has no limiting factor and cannot be sustained; logistic growth slows as the population approaches carrying capacity.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Differential equation forms, intrinsic rate of increase, and age-structured models are beyond this course.
relationships: A population grows exponentially when resources are effectively unlimited, with growth rate proportional to population size.
As resources become limiting, per-individual growth rate declines and the curve levels off near the carrying capacity.
No real population grows exponentially indefinitely, because no environment supplies unlimited resources.

Claiming predators normally drive their prey to extinction.
Claiming competition occurs only between members of different species.
fixed_facts: In mutualism both species benefit; in commensalism one benefits and the other is essentially unaffected; in parasitism and predation one benefits at the other's expense; in competition both are harmed.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Competitive exclusion modelling and niche partitioning theory in depth are beyond this course.
relationships: Interactions are classified by the effect on each participant, not by intent or by how the relationship appears.
Interspecific competition occurs where species use the same limiting resource, and it can shift the resources each species uses.
Predator and prey populations influence one another, typically with a delay between the change in one and the response of the other.

Genes close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together.

Variation is present in a population before selection acts on it.

disqualifying_errors: Modelling a continuously varying trait such as height as a single gene with two alleles and presenting the result as established.
Claiming genotype fully determines phenotype regardless of environment.
Claiming an environmentally induced change in an individual is inherited through the genome.
fixed_facts: Many traits are influenced by multiple genes and by the environment, and these show continuous rather than discrete variation.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Heritability estimation, quantitative trait loci, and genome-wide association methods are beyond this course.
relationships: A polygenic trait is influenced by several genes, each contributing part of the effect, which produces a continuous range of phenotypes.
The environment modifies the expression of many traits, so genotype does not determine phenotype on its own.
Simple dominant-recessive models apply to a minority of traits and mislead when applied to polygenic ones.

hazards.description: Collecting leaves without identifying the plant risks irritant sap, poison ivy, oak or sumac, and pesticide residue.
hazards.mitigation: Collect only from a plant an adult has identified as safe. Never from a plant with milky sap, never poison ivy, oak, or sumac, and never from a plant or verge that has been treated with pesticide. Wear gloves and wash hands afterwards.

hazards.description: Small counters and dried beans are a choking hazard around young children and are no longer food.
hazards.mitigation: Keep counters away from younger siblings, count them back into a labelled container, and never return them to food storage or eat them.

hazards.description: Family trait or pedigree work can expose genetic and health information about relatives who never consented.
hazards.mitigation: This unit uses NON-HUMAN specimens and fictional pedigrees only. The learner is never asked to record family traits, family medical history, ancestry, or any relative's data.

hazards.description: Heredity topics can touch on disability, adoption, or family history painfully.
hazards.mitigation: All examples are fictional or non-human; the learner may decline any example without penalty and no personal disclosure is ever requested.

safety_brief.h3_safety_segment_verbatim:

HAZARD (physical): Collecting leaves without identifying the plant risks irritant sap, poison ivy, oak or sumac, and pesticide residue.
MITIGATION: Collect only from a plant an adult has identified as safe. Never from a plant with milky sap, never poison ivy, oak, or sumac, and never from a plant or verge that has been treated with pesticide. Wear gloves and wash hands afterwards.
HAZARD (physical): Small counters and dried beans are a choking hazard around young children and are no longer food.
MITIGATION: Keep counters away from younger siblings, count them back into a labelled container, and never return them to food storage or eat them.
HAZARD (privacy): Family trait or pedigree work can expose genetic and health information about relatives who never consented.
MITIGATION: This unit uses NON-HUMAN specimens and fictional pedigrees only. The learner is never asked to record family traits, family medical history, ancestry, or any relative's data.
HAZARD (emotional): Heredity topics can touch on disability, adoption, or family history painfully.
MITIGATION: All examples are fictional or non-human; the learner may decline any example without penalty and no personal disclosure is ever requested.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.

  SAFE ORDER 3. Measure and record each of the 30 or more specimens before any grouping or graphing.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Run the coin or dice probability trials separately, recording every trial including the ones that look wrong.
  SAFE ORDER 5. No family trait, photograph, pedigree, or medical detail is collected at any point.

  STOP: Stop and use fictional data if any prompt seems to ask for real family information; it should not.

disqualifying_errors: Using gene and allele as interchangeable terms.
Claiming homologous chromosomes carry identical DNA sequences.
Claiming every gene is on a different chromosome from every other.
fixed_facts: A gene occupies a specific locus on a specific chromosome, and different versions of a gene at that locus are alleles.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Linkage mapping, recombination frequencies, and chromosome banding are beyond this course.
relationships: Genes occupy fixed positions on chromosomes, and homologous chromosomes carry the same genes at the same loci.
Diploid organisms carry two copies of each locus, one from each parent, and those copies may be the same allele or different alleles.
Genes close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming recombination creates new alleles.
Claiming variation arises in response to environmental need.
Claiming asexual reproduction produces the same level of genetic variety as sexual reproduction.
fixed_facts: The sources of heritable variation are mutation, recombination during meiosis, independent assortment, and the random combination of gametes at fertilisation.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Population genetics and allele frequency mathematics are beyond this course.
relationships: Mutation is the ultimate source of new alleles; the other mechanisms rearrange existing alleles into new combinations.
Sexual reproduction generates far more genetic variety among offspring than asexual reproduction does.
Variation is present in a population before selection acts on it.

disqualifying_errors: Reading a three-to-one expected ratio as a guarantee about four offspring.
Claiming previous offspring change the probability for a subsequent one.
Rejecting a genetic model because a small family departed from the expected ratio.
fixed_facts: A Punnett square gives expected proportions across many offspring, not an outcome for any individual offspring.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit testing is beyond this course.
relationships: A Punnett square enumerates the possible gamete combinations and their expected frequencies.
Each fertilisation is an independent event, so previous offspring do not change the probabilities for the next.
Observed proportions in small samples deviate from expectation by chance, and that deviation is not evidence against the model.

disqualifying_errors: Modelling a continuously varying trait such as height as a single gene with two alleles and presenting the result as established.
Claiming genotype fully determines phenotype regardless of environment.
Claiming an environmentally induced change in an individual is inherited through the genome.
fixed_facts: Many traits are influenced by multiple genes and by the environment, and these show continuous rather than discrete variation.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Heritability estimation, quantitative trait loci, and genome-wide association methods are beyond this course.
relationships: A polygenic trait is influenced by several genes, each contributing part of the effect, which produces a continuous range of phenotypes.
The environment modifies the expression of many traits, so genotype does not determine phenotype on its own.
Simple dominant-recessive models apply to a minority of traits and mislead when applied to polygenic ones.

disqualifying_errors: Inferring selection from a change in one individual.
Claiming a shift in a trait distribution is necessarily due to selection, without considering other causes.
Reporting a distributional change with no reference to sample size or generations.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Selection coefficients and formal statistical inference are beyond this course.
relationships: Selection is detected as a change in the distribution of a trait in a population over generations.
A shift in a distribution is evidence about the population, not about any individual within it.
The strength of the evidence depends on sample size, on measurement method, and on the number of generations observed.

disqualifying_errors: Describing an individual organism as adapting to its environment during its lifetime as an evolutionary process.
Claiming every trait an organism has is an adaptation.
Claiming an adaptation is a trait the organism developed because it was needed.
fixed_facts: Adaptation is a population-level outcome across generations, not a change an individual makes during its life.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Adaptationist critique, exaptation theory, and comparative methods are beyond this course.
relationships: An adaptation is a heritable trait that has become common in a population because it improved survival and reproduction in that environment.
A trait that is adaptive in one environment can be neutral or harmful in another, so adaptation is always relative to conditions.
Not every trait is an adaptation; some persist through chance, through linkage to other traits, or as by-products.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming a population will always evolve in time to survive an environmental change.
Claiming extinction indicates a defect in the organisms rather than a mismatch with changed conditions.
Claiming populations can evolve traits for which no variation exists.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Extinction rate estimation and mass extinction mechanisms in detail are beyond this course.
relationships: When the environment changes, populations may shift in trait frequency, migrate, or become extinct, and which occurs depends on existing variation and the rate of change.
Rapid change is more likely to cause extinction than gradual change, because there is less opportunity for trait frequencies to shift.
Extinction is the normal fate of most species over geological time, and the fossil record documents this.
